thread:
jules: FYI incoming escalation from Acme. They reported p99 latency jumping ~3x starting ~2024-04-12 09:50 UTC in us-west1. They say API timeouts + higher bill for retries. Dashboard shows p99 spike, but our rollup panel is flatter. Can someone triage?

samir: Noted. Do we have trace IDs or example request IDs from the customer?

jules: Sent a few in the ticket: req-0a1b2c3d, req-0a1b2c3e. They also pasted this curl causing a 504: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'`

maria: Running quick query against clickhouse histograms. Our rollup job (quantile_rollup_v2) publishes 5m-window p99; the raw trace-derived p99 (3s bins) shows spikes at 09:50-10:10. Possible sampling/aggregation mismatch.

maria: Query I ran: ```sql
SELECT toStartOfFiveMinute(timestamp) as t, quantileExact(0.99)(duration_ms) as p99
FROM api_latency_hist
WHERE region='us-west1' AND timestamp >= '2024-04-12 09:00'
GROUP BY t ORDER BY t
```

dex: We pushed a change to autoscaler/burst-policy at 2024-04-12T09:48 (release-bot: deploy 2024-04-12 09:48 by dex). That policy increased scale-down aggressiveness to free GPUs faster. Might explain transient queueing on cold starts.

samir: Could be. Customer traces show long queue times before execution for the spike windows. Can someone check instance churn and cold-start counts around 09:45-10:15?

maria: I pulled churn: increased instance termination events from 09:42-09:50, then several new pods 09:49-09:56. Also observe queue_time_ms distribution shifted right during 09:50-09:55.

jules: Customer says retries doubled their billed tokens due to timeouts. We need quick mitigation and a postmortem plan.

dex: Mitigation options: 1) revert aggressive scale-down (quick), 2) temporarily pin Acme to dedicated capacity or reserved pool, 3) bump min-instances for us-west1 to reduce churn. I can revert scale-down in ~5m if ops agrees.

samir: Before revert, can we confirm metric mismatch: why does our dashboard panel (prod/latency/p99-panel) show smaller spike than traces? Maria?

maria: Dashboard is reading from rollup table quantile_rollup_v2 with sampling_rate=0.1 and a 5m aggregation window; that smooths out short spikes. Traces and raw histograms use per-request timings so they show true instantaneous p99. Dashboard confusion = sampling + aggregation.

samir: That explains user-facing p99 disagreement. Need to annotate dashboard or change panel to use raw/higher-res source for SLO pages. Also add runbook: when customer reports p99 spike, check raw traces + instance churn.

jules: For immediate action: Dex, please revert autoscaler policy. Maria, update dashboard annotation that rollup uses 5m sampling and may underreport sub-window spikes. Samir, can you draft an internal alert to surface instance churn correlated with p99 so engineering gets paged?

dex: Reverting now. Command I used: `kubectl apply -f autoscaler/policies/scale-down-2024-04-08.yaml -n runtime` — will watch.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started by dex at 2024-04-12T10:01:05Z.

maria: After rollback, early signs look better: queue_time_ms back to baseline by 10:08, new traces show p99 trending down. I'll run the higher-res p99 panel and post results.

samir: I'll open a short incident ticket and assign owners: root cause hypothesis = aggressive scale-down + rollup aggregation hiding spikes; mitigations = revert, bump min-instances, update dashboards and runbooks, consider dedicated pool for high-SLA customers.

jules: Thanks. I'll update Acme with progress and offer a temporary credit for retry charges. Keep me posted.

maria: Posting follow-up p99 table (raw 1m bins): ```
09:44  p99=220ms
09:50  p99=1850ms
09:52  p99=2100ms
09:56  p99=340ms
```

dex: Rollback completed at 10:07 UTC. ops-bot shows no further terminations after 10:05.

samir: Nice work. Action items: Maria to update dashboard text + add a 1m-resolution SLO panel; Dex to propose autoscaler policy that respects a min-instance floor for latency-critical tiers; Jules to coordinate customer communication and credits. Closing thread when tickets created. :thumbsup:
